name: Sepp Blatter
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Blatter was working as head of public relations for the Valais Tourist Board (1959-1964) and had recently graduated from the University of Lausanne. His FIFA career began at age 39 in 1975, and he became FIFA president in 1998 at age 62.
early_history_summary: Blatter was born in Visp, Switzerland, the son of a chemical factory worker. He earned a degree in business and economics from the University of Lausanne in 1959, then worked in PR for the Valais Tourist Board before becoming general secretary of the Swiss Ice Hockey Federation in 1964. He joined FIFA as technical director in 1975 at age 39.
family_context_summary: Son of a chemical factory worker in Visp, Switzerland. Not documented as having significant financial or domain advantages.
evidence_summary: Blatter's early career consisted of routine PR and administrative roles in Swiss tourism and ice hockey. His material career milestones all came after age 39 when he joined FIFA in 1975. No independently verifiable material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Boris Berezovsky
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Berezovsky was working as a research engineer at the Institute of Control Sciences of the USSR Academy of Sciences. His business career began in 1989 at age 43 with LogoVAZ, and his political influence came in the mid-1990s.
early_history_summary: Berezovsky was born in Moscow to a civil engineer father and a pediatric nurse mother. He graduated from the Moscow Forestry Engineering Institute in 1968 and worked as an engineer and research officer at the Institute of Control Sciences from 1969 to 1987, publishing scientific papers from 1975. He earned his doctorate in 1983 at age 37. His business career began only after perestroika in 1989.
family_context_summary: Son of a civil engineer and a pediatric nurse in Moscow. The family lived modestly; Berezovsky later recalled sharing a Zhiguli car with a friend at age 42.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a civil engineer in construction; not directly related to Berezovsky's eventual business or mathematical career.
evidence_summary: Berezovsky's early career was as a research engineer and mathematician in the Soviet academic system. He published scientific papers from 1975 onward but achieved no material milestone by age 26. His oligarch-level business success came entirely after age 43, enabled by post-Soviet privatization rather than early-career achievements.

name: Sofia Gubaidulina
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Gubaidulina was a student at the Moscow Conservatory studying composition (1954-1959/1961). Her first notable work, Concordanza, came in 1970 at age 39, and her international breakthrough with Offertorium came in 1980 at age 49.
early_history_summary: Gubaidulina was born in Chistopol, Tatar ASSR, to a surveyor/engineer father of Volga Tatar origin and a teacher mother of Polish-Jewish descent. She discovered music at age five, studied at the Kazan Conservatory (graduating 1954), then pursued composition at the Moscow Conservatory from 1954 to 1959, continuing as a postgraduate under Vissarion Shebalin until 1961. During her early career she supported herself writing film scores while developing her own voice.
family_context_summary: Father was a surveyor and engineer of Volga Tatar origin; mother was a teacher of Polish-Jewish descent. Not documented as having significant financial or musical family advantages.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having musical family background.
evidence_summary: Gubaidulina was still a conservatory student at age 26, with no independently verifiable material milestone. Her works were rarely performed in the Soviet Union early on, and she supported herself with film scores. Her first striking compositional voice emerged with Concordanza in 1970 at age 39, and her international breakthrough came with Offertorium in 1980.

name: Takeshi Kitano
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Kitano formed the comedy duo 'Two Beat' in 1973 at age 26, but national fame came in the late 1970s and 1980s through TV shows. His film career began with Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence (1983) at age 36, and his directorial debut was Violent Cop (1989) at age 42.
early_history_summary: Kitano was born in Adachi, Tokyo, the youngest of four children in a working-class family. His father was a house painter with yakuza-like behavior, and his mother was a strict factory worker who pushed education. He entered Meiji University to study engineering but dropped out. He worked as an elevator boy and emcee at the France-za strip theater in Asakusa, learning comedy from comedian Senzaburo Fukami, before forming the manzai duo Two Beat with Kiyoshi Kaneko in 1973.
family_context_summary: Working-class family in Adachi, Tokyo. Father was a house painter; mother was a factory worker and strict disciplinarian who valued education. Not documented as having financial or entertainment industry advantages.
evidence_summary: Kitano's early career involved menial work and apprenticeship at a strip theater before forming a comedy duo at age 26. While he learned comedy skills from Senzaburo Fukami, the duo's national fame came years later in the late 1970s and 1980s. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found; forming a comedy duo is not itself a material milestone.

name: Toshihide Maskawa
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Maskawa was a graduate student at Nagoya University. He earned his PhD in 1967 at age 27, and his Nobel Prize-winning Kobayashi-Maskawa paper was published in 1973 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Maskawa was born in Nagoya, Japan, to parents who were sugar merchants. He had a weak constitution as a child and was raised largely among adults. He entered Nagoya University in 1958, motivated by a desire to avoid becoming a sugar merchant. He joined the particle-theory group of Shoichi Sakata and earned his PhD in 1967. He spent three years as a postdoc at Nagoya before moving to Kyoto University in 1970 as an assistant professor. His Nobel-winning collaboration with Makoto Kobayashi began in 1972.
family_context_summary: Parents were small business owners trading sugar in Nagoya. They worked long hours and did not closely supervise children's studies. Not documented as having significant financial or academic advantages.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were sugar merchants; not connected to physics or academia.
evidence_summary: Maskawa was a graduate student at Nagoya University at age 26 with no material milestone. His PhD came at 27, and his Nobel Prize-winning work on CP violation and quark families was published at age 33 in 1973. His early path was shaped by self-directed study and the Sakata particle-theory group, but no independently verifiable material achievement occurred by age 26.

name: Neil Young
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the influential folk-rock band Buffalo Springfield in 1966 at age 20, then launched a major solo career with 'Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere' (1969, age 23) and the chart-topping 'Harvest' (1972, age 26), establishing him as an international rock star well before 26.
early_history_summary: Young was born in Toronto to Scott Young, a well-known Canadian journalist and sportswriter, and Rassy Young. His parents divorced when he was 12, and he moved with his mother to Winnipeg. He began playing music as a teen, forming bands like The Jades and The Squires in the early 1960s. He played the Winnipeg community club circuit and Toronto coffeehouses before moving to Los Angeles in 1966 to form Buffalo Springfield with Stephen Stills and Richie Furay.
family_context_summary: Son of Scott Young, a prominent Canadian journalist and sportswriter, and Rassy Young. Parents divorced when Neil was 12; he moved with his mother to a working-class area of Winnipeg. Father's cultural capital provided exposure to media and arts but not direct music industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: LA music scene, folk-rock wave, Stephen Stills collaboration, teen band reps, parental divorce
evidence_summary: Young began playing in bands as a teenager in Winnipeg, building several years of performing experience before moving to Los Angeles in 1966 at age 20 to co-found Buffalo Springfield. His father was a well-known journalist providing cultural capital but not music-specific advantages. The move to LA placed him at the epicenter of the 1960s folk-rock movement, and his partnerships with Stephen Stills and later Crosby, Stills, and Nash provided elite collaborative networks. By age 26 he had released multiple major-label albums including the chart-topping 'Harvest.'

name: Ismail Kadare
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first poetry collection 'Frymezimet djaloshare' (Youthful Inspirations) in 1954 at age 18, followed by multiple collections through 1961 including 'Shekulli im' (My Century, 1961) at age 25, establishing him as a leading young literary voice in Albania well before 26.
early_history_summary: Kadare was born in Gjirokaster, Albania, to a post office employee father and a homemaker mother. He attended primary and secondary schools in Gjirokaster, then studied Languages and Literature at the University of Tirana, receiving a teacher's diploma in 1956. He continued studies at the Gorky Institute of World Literature in Moscow from 1958 to 1960 before returning to Tirana when Albania-Soviet relations soured. He published poetry from age 18 and became an established writer in Albania through the late 1950s.
family_context_summary: Father was a post office employee in Gjirokaster; mother was a homemaker. Modest background with no documented financial or literary family advantages. Maternal great-grandfather was a Bektashi poet (Bejtexhi), suggesting some cultural heritage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early publication, Gjirokaster heritage, Soviet-Albanian political turmoil, state literary system, poetic talent
evidence_summary: Kadare published his first poetry collection at age 18 and became an established literary voice in Albania by his mid-twenties, with multiple collections including 'Shekulli im' (1961). He grew up in Gjirokaster under fascist occupation and then Stalinist rule, with a modest family background. His education at the University of Tirana and the Gorky Institute in Moscow provided literary training, but his early publication record was driven by his own talent and the constraints of the Albanian state literary system. The extreme political environment of communist Albania shaped his literary voice from a young age.

name: France Gall
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1965 at age 17 with 'Poupee de cire, poupee de son,' and had multiple hit singles throughout the 1960s, making her one of France's biggest yé-yé pop stars well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Gall was born in Paris to Robert Gall, a lyricist who wrote for Edith Piaf and Charles Aznavour, and Cecile Berthier, a singer whose father co-founded the celebrated choir The Little Singers of Paris. She began playing piano and guitar at age five. Her father encouraged her career, taking her to studios and concert halls from a young age. She signed with Philips Records in 1963 at age 15 after auditioning at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees. Her debut single 'Ne sois pas si bete' aired on her 16th birthday and sold 200,000 copies. Serge Gainsbourg wrote songs for her, including the Eurovision-winning entry.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent French music family. Father Robert Gall was a lyricist for Edith Piaf and Charles Aznavour. Mother Cecile Berthier was a singer; maternal grandfather Paul Berthier co-founded The Little Singers of Paris choir. She was a fixture backstage at the Paris Olympia from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father lyricist, Piaf connection, Philips Records, Eurovision, Gainsbourg, Paris Olympia, yé-yé wave
evidence_summary: Gall's career was profoundly shaped by her family's deep roots in the French music industry. Her father was a lyricist for major stars, her mother was a singer, and her grandfather founded a famous choir. She was taken backstage at the Paris Olympia as a child and signed to Philips Records at 15 through her father's industry connections. By 17 she won Eurovision, and by 26 she was one of France's most beloved pop stars. The yé-yé wave of the 1960s provided a structural tailwind, and Gainsbourg's songwriting was a key complementary partnership.

name: Mikhail Tal
milestone_by_age_26: Became a chess grandmaster in 1957 at age 21, won the Soviet Championship in 1957 and 1958, and became World Chess Champion in 1960 at age 23 — the youngest world champion in history at that time — all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Tal was born in Riga, Latvia, into a Jewish family. His father was a medical doctor. Tal learned chess at age seven by watching his father, and joined the Riga Palace of Young Pioneers chess club. At age 12, he began training with Alexander Koblents, after which his game rapidly improved. He won his first Latvian Championship at age 16 in 1953, qualified for the USSR Championship in 1956, and won the Soviet Championship in 1957 at age 21, becoming the youngest player to do so. FIDE awarded him the grandmaster title that same year. He won the Candidates Tournament in 1959 and defeated Mikhail Botvinnik in 1960 to become World Champion at age 23.
primary_leverage_engine: Chess talent and early intensive training
family_context_summary: Born into a Jewish family in Riga, Latvia. Father was a medical doctor. Not documented as having significant financial advantages, but the family supported his chess development. Had chronic health problems from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess system, Koblents training, Riga Pioneers club, prodigy talent, Jewish identity, health adversity
evidence_summary: Tal's extraordinary chess talent was evident from childhood; he won against a master at age 13 in a simultaneous exhibition. The Soviet chess pipeline provided structured access to competitive play through the Riga Palace of Young Pioneers, and trainer Alexander Koblents provided sustained individualized coaching from age 12. Tal won the Latvian Championship at 16, became a grandmaster at 21, and World Champion at 23. His chronic health problems and Jewish identity in Soviet Latvia created adversity, but his prodigy-level talent and the elite Soviet chess ecosystem were the dominant factors in his early success.

name: Rosalind Franklin
milestone_by_age_26: Earned a PhD from Cambridge University in 1945 at age 25 and published multiple foundational research papers on the physical structure of coal and graphite through the British Coal Utilisation Research Association, making recognized scientific contributions before age 26.
early_history_summary: Franklin was born in London to a prominent Anglo-Jewish family. Her father Ellis Franklin was a partner at Keyser's Bank. She attended St. Paul's School for Girls, which emphasized science education, and knew she wanted to be a scientist by age 15. She entered Newnham College, Cambridge in 1938 to study physical chemistry, graduating in 1941. She worked at the British Coal Utilisation Research Association (BCURA) from 1942 to 1947, publishing several papers on coal structure that earned her a PhD in 1945. She then moved to Paris to learn X-ray diffraction techniques before joining King's College London in 1951.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Anglo-Jewish family in London. Father was a partner at Keyser's Bank; family businesses included publishing (Routledge & Kegan Paul). Both parents active in community services. The family was well-to-do and supported her education, though her father initially discouraged her scientific ambitions.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge, St Paul's Girls, BCURA, Anglo-Jewish family, banking family, gender barriers, early science aptitude
evidence_summary: Franklin's path to a PhD by age 25 was enabled by her prominent Anglo-Jewish family's financial stability, elite schooling at St. Paul's School for Girls, and admission to Newnham College, Cambridge. Her father was a banker, providing a strong financial platform, though he initially discouraged her scientific career. Her research at BCURA on coal structure produced multiple published papers and a PhD by 1945. Gender barriers in mid-century British science created adversity, but her family's resources and the Cambridge academic pipeline were the dominant early advantages.

name: Antonio Conte
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Lecce at age 16 in April 1986, joined Juventus in 1991 at age 22, and won the UEFA Cup (1993), Serie A title (1995), and Coppa Italia (1995) with Juventus — multiple major trophies before age 26.
early_history_summary: Conte was born in Lecce, Italy, and joined his hometown club Lecce's youth academy in 1982 at age 13. He made his Serie A debut on April 6, 1986 at age 16, becoming one of the youngest players in Lecce's history. Under manager Carlo Mazzone, he became a fundamental player. He suffered a tibia fracture in 1987 that risked ending his career. He joined Juventus in 1991 at age 22 under Giovanni Trapattoni, becoming a key midfielder and eventually team captain, winning multiple trophies over 13 seasons.
family_context_summary: Born in Lecce, Italy. Not documented as having significant financial or football family advantages. His hometown club provided the entry point to professional football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lecce youth academy, Juventus, Serie A debut at 16, Mazzone, Trapattoni, tibia fracture, Italian football
evidence_summary: Conte's early career was built on joining his hometown club Lecce's youth academy at 13 and making his Serie A debut at 16, an unusually early professional start. The Italian football system, one of the world's strongest leagues, provided an elite performance pipeline. His move to Juventus at 22 placed him at one of Europe's top clubs with elite teammates. A tibia fracture at 18 created significant adversity. Managers Carlo Mazzone and Giovanni Trapattoni provided early mentorship. By 26, he had won multiple major trophies including the UEFA Cup and Serie A title.

name: Giuseppe Tornatore
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Tornatore made a documentary that won a Salerno Festival prize and worked for RAI before 26, but his first feature film 'Il Camorrista' (The Professor) came in 1985 at age 29, and his Oscar-winning 'Cinema Paradiso' came in 1988 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Tornatore was born in Bagheria, Sicily. He developed an interest in theatre from age 16, staging works by Pirandello and De Filippo. He worked as a freelance photographer before switching to cinema, making his debut with a documentary on ethnic minorities in Sicily that won a Salerno Festival prize. He then worked for RAI before his first feature film in 1985 at age 29, which won the Silver Ribbon for best new director. His breakthrough came with Cinema Paradiso (1988), which won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 1990.
family_context_summary: Born in Bagheria, near Palermo, Sicily. Not documented as having significant financial or film industry family advantages.
evidence_summary: Tornatore's early career involved theatre, photography, and a documentary that won a minor festival prize, plus work at RAI. However, his first feature film came at age 29 and his career-defining work (Cinema Paradiso) at age 32. The Salerno Festival documentary prize is not a material milestone comparable to his later achievements. No independently verifiable material milestone by age 26 was found.
